question: For which of the following patients would you recommend prophylaxis against mycobacterium avium-intracellulare?

options.opa: 22-year old HIV positive female with CD4 count of 750 cells/ microliter and a viral load of 500,000 copies/mL
options.opb: 30-year old HIV positive male with CD4 count of 20 cells/ microliter and a viral load of < 50 copies/mL
options.opc: 45-year old HIV positive female with CD4 count of 250 cells/ microliter and a viral load of 100,000 copies/mL
options.opd: 50-year old HIV positive female with CD4 count of 150 cells/ microliter and a viral load of < 50 copies/mL
options.ope: 36-year old HIV positive male with CD4 count of 75 cells/microliter and an undetectable viral load.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Low CD4 count -> increased risk of opportunistic infections -> Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare prophylaxis recommended -> 95%
CHAIN: High viral load -> increased risk of opportunistic infections -> Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare prophylaxis recommended -> 90%
CHAIN: CD4 count < 50 cells/microliter -> significantly increased risk of opportunistic infections -> Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare prophylaxis recommended -> 98%
CHAIN: Undetectable viral load -> reduced risk of opportunistic infections -> Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare prophylaxis may not be necessary -> 70%
enhanced_information: Prophylaxis against Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare is recommended for patients with low CD4 counts (<50 cells/microliter) due to significantly increased risk of opportunistic infections. This recommendation is supported by the consensus that low CD4 counts increase susceptibility to opportunistic infections, including Mycobacterium avium Complex. Therefore, the 30-year old HIV positive male with a CD4 count of 20 cells/microliter (option b) would benefit from prophylaxis.
analysis: Prophylaxis against Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare is recommended for patients with low CD4 counts (<50 cells/microliter) due to significantly increased risk of opportunistic infections. The 30-year old HIV positive male with a CD4 count of 20 cells/microliter (option b) falls into this category and would benefit from prophylaxis.
